To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nicotine upregulated expression of TH, DBH, PNMT, PAM, and neuropeptidY genes in the rat adrenal gland.

the expression of catecholine-synthesizing enzyme genes in the adrenal medullae of rats is increased by nicotine treatment and that this increase is paralleled by an increase in neuropeptide Y and peptidyl-glycine α-amino monooxygenase mRNA.

nicotine upregulates the expression of TH and PNMT in the adrenal medullary chromaffin cells and that the upregulation of these enzymes is paralleled by an upregulation in the expression of neuropeptide Y, the main neuropeptide of the adrenal medulla, and by the expression of its processing enzyme, peptidylecaine α-amidating monoxygenase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms by which the adrenal medulla responds to stress.
the regulation of the adrenal medulla by the sympathetic nervous system, which is a major component of the stress response.
the effects of stress on the synthesis of catecholamines and neuropeptides in the adrenal medullary cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of catech olamine-synthesising enzymes, PAM, and the neuropept ide NPY mRNA in rat adrenal medulla are regulated in parallel by acute systemic nicotine.
the catecholamine synthesizing enzyme genes, PAM, and the NPY gene are all upregulated in the adrenal medullary cells by nicotine.

the expression of catecholine-synthesizing enzyme genes, the neuropeptide NPY, and the peptidyl-glycine α-aminoating monooxygenases are regulated in parallel after acute systemic administration of nicotine in the rat adrenal gland.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nicotine upregulates catecholamine synthesis, and that this upregulation is paralleled by an upregulation in neuropeptide synthesis.

the expression of catech olamine and peptide genes in the adrenal medullary chromaffin cells is increased by nicotine treatment, but that the increase in the expression of the peptide genes is smaller than that of catecholaminergic genes.
catecholamine enzymes and NPY are upregulated in parallel, whereas PAM is not, by nicotinic receptor stimulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adrenal medulla, which is known as the “fight or flight” organ, is activated by stress.
the expression of catecholine and neuropeptide genes is upregulated by a common mechanism in the adrenal medullary cells after nicotine administration.
the adrenal medulla has an important role in stress response and that this role is mediated in part by neuropeptides.
